open_obligations: Check that the 'prior strategy from [2]' in Table 9 matches the answer-extraction code actually used by Du et al.
Check whether Du et al.'s majority-vote baseline is comparable to the authors' T = 0 majority voting over 5 agents
Confirm the critique is shown only on GSM8K with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and not on Du et al.'s ChatGPT setting
out.other_title: Multiagent debate beats single agent, reflection and majority vote on arithmetic and GSM8K
out.rationale: Du et al. report that multiagent debate beats single-agent, reflection and majority-vote baselines on arithmetic and GSM8K; the authors argue this evaluation is confounded by answer parsing. They back the argument with one GSM8K comparison (Table 9, p25 L211-216, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) where single-agent accuracy under their extraction exceeds MAD scored with Du et al.'s strategy, so this is a methodological critique rather than a rerun of Du et al.'s ChatGPT experiments.
out.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Whether MAD's reported advantage over majority voting and single agents survives a standardized final-answer extraction protocol

text: The authors note that prior works, including Du et al., reported consistent gains from multi-agent debate over majority voting, and argue that these results may be partially driven by error-prone rule-based answer extraction that marks correct responses as incorrect.
title: Choi et al. argue Du et al.'s reported MAD gains over majority voting partly reflect answer parsing
